html:
The forced march of the whole population of Phnom Penh into the countryside by the Khmer Rouge, starting on the day they took the city, 17 April 1975.

Years of civil war and American bombing had swollen the capital with refugees to perhaps two million people. Within hours of marching in, Khmer Rouge soldiers ordered everyone out, saying the Americans would bomb the city and people could return in three days. Hospitals were emptied, and the sick were pushed along in their beds. Those who refused were shot. Other towns were cleared the same way.

Pol Pot's regime wanted a nation of peasants with no cities, money or markets, starting again from "Year Zero". City people became "new people", the lowest class in the labour camps. Former officials, soldiers, teachers and the educated were singled out for death.

The march was the first act of the Cambodian genocide. By the time the Vietnamese invasion ended Khmer Rouge rule in January 1979, about two million people, roughly a quarter of Cambodia, had died of execution, starvation and disease.
sum: The forced march of the whole population of Phnom Penh into the countryside by the Khmer Rouge, starting on the day they took the city, 17 April 1975.
